script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: a shadow can't outrun what makes it. The Moon's shadow crossed America in 90 minutes, faster than the Concorde ever flew. That's real.

science.claim: A shadow can't outrun what makes it.
science.working: A shadow edge exists only where light is being blocked, so it cannot outrun the light that draws it. Any change in a shadow - the edge jumping as the blocker or the lamp moves - propagates from the blocker at the speed of light, c = 299,792,458 m/s, the physical speed limit for anything that carries information. A shadow that moves ahead of its light isn't a shadow: the rule is what makes the cost real.
science.source: geometrical optics (a shadow is the projection of the blocker's silhouette); special relativity (nothing carrying information exceeds c)

science.claim: The Moon's shadow crossed America in 90 minutes, faster than the Concorde ever flew.
science.working: The 21 August 2017 total solar eclipse: the Moon's umbra entered the United States at Madras, Oregon at about 17:19 UTC and left the coast near Charleston, South Carolina at about 18:49 UTC, roughly 90 minutes from coast to coast over a ground path of about 4,000 km. 4,000 km / 1.5 h is about 2,700 km/h on average (faster mid-track). Concorde cruised at about 2,180 km/h (Mach 2.05); even its record 30 June 1973 eclipse flight ran at about 2,150 km/h and held totality for 74 minutes. The ground shadow beat the fastest passenger jet ever flown.
science.source: NASA, total solar eclipse of 21 August 2017; Concorde 001's solar-eclipse flight, 30 June 1973 (Mach 2.05, 74 minutes of totality)
